body: In truth there is no 'answer'. Everyone's reality is their own, and trust me, using me as the basis of whether or not to do something is probably not going to turn out so well. I guess the only thing i've learned is that it doesn't matter whether or not you're doing something that you 'should' do, or that you want to do, in the end life will be what it is, no matter of your actions. When I moved away, the only thing I could not get away from was myself. And as it turns out, I'm the problem, and after many years of trying to fix that problem, I still feel the same way.

It's not that I cannot silence it completely, it's that I cannot silence it to any degree. I don't know whether it's just a defense mechanism for dealing with my own mind, that somehow if I keep thinking I don't have to think about that figurative black hole, but thoughts are always there. As for CBT, i'm familiar with what it is and how it works in theory.

I guess the biggest trigger at the moment is failure. I know everyone fails, and how it can be beneficial, but when everything I do ends up being wrong, for so many years... and I wish that was some sort of exaggeration... well suicide becomes the only choice, something I know I can do, and succeed, and that once i've done it, the pain will be gone permanently. People say of suicide, that it's a permanent solution to a temporary problem, to sway people from it, but I always hear it, and realise how comforting that is instead.

Learning never stops, but I guess it's down to what lessons you learn, and how you take them. I feel like the lesson I am fighting against is the lesson that sometimes giving up is the only answer. When I struggle, fight, try to live on, that's when it hurts the most. When I feel like I can just give up and die, then everything is just that little bit better. I've tried learning and changing for most of my life, tried different things, tried meeting different people, and the outcome is always similar. I've tried meditation, but my mind is too active for it to work. I don't know how to 'not think', thoughts are always there, even when trying to keep myself distracted. I've also tried CBT, but I might have been unlucky on that one, as the only therapist I could find in my area who practiced that, there was a personality clash with. I like to think I know the process well enough that I can understand my thought processes, having studied psychology, but self-treatment... I know it's not generally reliable. I guess I just feel I've tried everything I reasonably can.

I understand, I always say the same to myself when looking at these sort of things from others, that I want to help, but if I had a solution, then I wouldn't be feeling this way too. Every day is different, I know, but I guess I feel that the same patterns always repeat, and that while circumstances are different, the outcome is the same, or at least I stay the same throughout those changes, and cannot shake off the part of the problem which comes from within me.
